title: DFIR Analyst
description: Investigate complex security breaches, perform digital forensics, analyze memory artifacts, preserve chain of custody, and remediate incidents.

goal.objective: Uncover the root cause of security incidents, extract forensic evidence from endpoints and memory, and guide organizations through emergency containment.

learn.summary: Master volatile memory extraction and analysis with Volatility, Windows forensic artifacts (MFT, Registry, Prefetch, Event Logs), disk imaging, and timeline analysis with Plaso.
key_competencies: Evidence Handling & Legal Chain of Custody

capstone_projects.title: End-to-End Ransomware Breach Investigation Case Study
capstone_projects.description: Analyze a memory dump and disk image of an infected machine, reconstruct the adversary timeline, identify the entry point, and write a forensic report.

capstone_projects.title: Ransomware Attack Forensic Investigation & Timeline Reconstruction
capstone_projects.description: Perform memory and disk forensics on a simulated compromised Windows workstation, isolating malware persistence mechanisms, extracting C2 IP addresses, and assembling an evidentiary timeline.

interview_focus: Prefetch Files vs Shimcache Evidence Value
Preserving Volatile RAM without Contaminating Evidence
Order of Volatility in Digital Forensics

tree.name: DFIR Fundamentals & Incident Response Lifecycle
tree.description: Establish a strong understanding of what DFIR work entails, its ethical and legal boundaries, and the structured approach to handling security incidents.

resources.title: NIST Incident Handling Guide SP 800-61 Rev. 2
What is Digital Forensics & Incident Response (DFIR)?
Incident Response Full Course - Learn to Protect Your Systems from Cyber Attacks

children.name: Incident Response Life Cycle & Frameworks
children.description: Deep dive into the stages of incident response (preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery, post-incident activity) as per NIST, SANS, and other industry frameworks. Understand playbooks and runbooks for structured incident management.

resources.title: Understanding the NIST Incident Response Life Cycle
Incident Response Playbooks: What Are They & How to Create One
What is an Incident Response Plan? (NIST 800-61 Explained)

children.name: Digital Forensics Principles & Evidence Handling
children.description: Understand the fundamental principles of digital forensics, the importance of chain of custody, proper evidence preservation techniques, legal and ethical considerations, and standardized reporting.

resources.title: ACPO Good Practice Guide for Digital Evidence
Digital Forensics for Beginners | Intro to Cybersecurity

children.name: DFIR Lab Setup & Essential Tooling
children.description: Setting up a secure and effective DFIR lab environment (virtual machines, forensic workstations). Introduction to essential tools for triage, forensic imaging (DD, E01), hashing for integrity verification, and write-blocking (hardware/software). Practical use of tools like FTK Imager, Autopsy, and KAPE.

resources.title: KAPE (Kroll Artifact Parser and Extractor) Documentation
How to set up a Digital Forensics Virtual Lab

children.name: Operating System Fundamentals for Forensics
children.description: Understand core operating system components critical for forensic analysis: processes, services, user accounts, file permissions, kernel modules, boot processes, and system architecture across Windows, Linux, and macOS environments.

resources.title: Operating System Full Course for Beginners
Linux Kernel Internals - A Crash Course

tree.name: Core Technical Skills & Implementation
tree.description: Develop hands-on expertise in various forensic disciplines to collect, analyze, and interpret digital evidence from diverse sources effectively.

resources.title: Digital Forensics Course - Learn the Basics of Computer Forensics

children.name: Live Response & Endpoint Triage
children.description: Learn techniques for collecting volatile data from active systems without disturbing ongoing operations. This includes capturing memory dumps, running processes, network connections, command history, and utilizing live response scripting and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tools for immediate incident investigation and containment.

resources.title: Introduction to Live Response with Kansa
Live Response for Incident Response & Threat Hunting
DFIR | Live Forensics | Windows Memory Forensics | Process Dumper | FTK Imager

children.name: Windows Host Forensics
children.description: Master forensic analysis of Windows systems, including detailed examination of file systems (NTFS, FAT), registry hive analysis, event logs, prefetch files, JumpLists, ShellBags, LNK files, ShimCache, Amcache, and MFT analysis. Understand common Windows artifacts related to user activity, execution, and persistence.

resources.title: The Windows Registry: A Forensic Perspective
Windows Forensics Crash Course Part 1 - Windows Artifacts
DFIR: Windows Host Forensics - Tools and Artifacts

children.name: Linux & macOS Host Forensics
children.description: Perform forensic investigations on Linux systems (Ext4, system logs, Bash history, process accounting, cron jobs, network configurations) and macOS (APFS, Unified Log, Plists, Time Machine backups, TCC database, browser artifacts, Spotlight metadata).

resources.title: macOS Incident Response and Forensics with Phil Hagen

children.name: File System Forensics Deep Dive
children.description: A dedicated exploration of common file systems (NTFS, Ext4, APFS, HFS+), their structures, metadata, journaling mechanisms, and advanced artifact analysis like Master File Table (MFT) records, USN Journal, Volume Shadow Copies, and APFS snapshots. Understand deleted file recovery techniques.

resources.title: Digital Forensics and Incident Response: Mastering NTFS
Master File Table (MFT) Deep Dive | DFIR
Deep Dive into Linux Filesystems (ext4) and Forensics

children.name: Memory Forensics
children.description: Learn to acquire and analyze memory dumps using tools like Volatility and Rekall. Focus on extracting running processes, network connections, loaded DLLs, injected code, command history, user activity, and detecting rootkits or hidden processes.

children.name: Network Forensics & Packet Analysis
children.description: Analyze network traffic for indicators of compromise (IOCs). Understand common network protocols (TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP, SMB), use packet capture tools like Wireshark and TShark, interpret network flow data (NetFlow, IPFIX), and detect anomalies or malicious communication patterns.

resources.title: Wireshark Tutorial for Beginners - Network Analysis

children.name: Log Analysis & SIEM Fundamentals
children.description: Develop skills in parsing, filtering, and analyzing various log types (system, application, firewall, web server, cloud logs). Understand SIEM concepts, data ingestion, normalization, correlation rules, alert generation, and integration with threat intelligence. Gain practical experience with platforms like Splunk, ELK Stack, and Microsoft Sentinel, including query languages like KQL or SPL.

resources.title: The ELK Stack: A Deep Dive into Logs
Getting Started with SIEM | Security Information and Event Management Explained
ELK Stack Tutorial - ELK Stack Explained

tree.name: Advanced DFIR & Operational Excellence
tree.description: Transition from foundational skills to advanced enterprise-level incident response practices, proactive threat hunting, and specialized forensic areas like cloud, malware analysis, and automation.

resources.title: Digital Forensics & Incident Response (DFIR) Master Class (Prabh Nair)

children.name: Enterprise IR & SOAR Automation
children.description: Learn to manage and scale incident response within large organizations. Explore Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) platforms, develop playbooks for automated responses, and integrate with security tools via APIs to streamline operations.

resources.title: What is SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response)?
Python Automation Tutorial for Beginners (Full Course)

children.name: Threat Hunting & MITRE ATT&CK
children.description: Develop proactive threat hunting methodologies. Utilize threat intelligence and frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK to identify adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) that bypass traditional security controls, and build robust detection rules.

resources.title: Threat Hunting 101: What it is and How to get Started

children.name: Cloud & Container Forensics
children.description: Understand the unique challenges and techniques for performing forensics in cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP) including logging, snapshotting, API analysis, and cloud-native security tools. Explore incident response and forensics within containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes).

children.name: Malware Triage & Basic Analysis
children.description: Perform basic static analysis (file signatures, strings, packers, PE header analysis) and dynamic analysis (sandboxing, process monitoring, network traffic analysis) of suspicious executables, scripts, and documents to understand their behavior, extract indicators of compromise (IOCs), and write basic YARA rules for detection.

resources.title: REMnux: The Linux Toolkit for Reverse-Engineering and Malware Analysis
YARA: The Pattern Matching Swiss Knife for Malware Researchers
Malware Analysis Crash Course for Beginners
YARA Rules Tutorial For Beginners | Create & Test YARA Rules

children.name: Scripting for DFIR Automation
children.description: Develop essential scripting skills (Python, PowerShell, Bash) for automating repetitive DFIR tasks such as data parsing, log analysis, evidence collection, tool integration, and report generation. Focus on practical scripts for efficiency and scalability.

resources.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
Python Automation Tutorial for Beginners - Full Course
PowerShell for Beginners Course - Learn in 4 Hours

children.name: Email Forensics
children.description: Master techniques for analyzing email headers, body content, attachments, and links to investigate phishing attempts, Business Email Compromise (BEC), malware delivery vectors, and insider threats. Understand email protocols (SMTP, POP3, IMAP) and anti-spam technologies.

resources.title: Email Header Analysis For Phishing Investigations
Analyzing Phishing Emails with John Hammond

children.name: Advanced Threat Detection & Response
children.description: Explore advanced threat detection techniques, understanding sophisticated adversary tactics like Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs), supply chain attacks, and leveraging frameworks beyond MITRE ATT&CK for deeper incident analysis and response strategies. Focus on proactive hunting and innovative defense mechanisms.

resources.title: Advanced Persistent Threats: A Practical Guide
Cyber Security: Threat Hunting - Learn to hunt for threats in your network
What is an APT attack? (Advanced Persistent Threat)

tree.name: Portfolio & Career Readiness
tree.description: Transform theoretical knowledge and practical skills into demonstrable proof for career advancement. Focus on effective communication, professional development, and showcasing expertise.

resources.title: Building a Cybersecurity Portfolio (A Must-Have for Beginners)!
How to Get a Job in Cybersecurity (Tips, Tricks & Resources)

children.name: Incident Reporting & Stakeholder Communication
children.description: Master the art of crafting clear, concise, and actionable incident reports. Learn to effectively communicate findings and recommendations to technical teams, management, legal counsel, and other stakeholders.

resources.title: Cyber Security Incident Response: Communication Plan

children.name: DFIR Capstone Project: End-to-End Incident Simulation
children.description: Apply all learned skills in a comprehensive, simulated incident response scenario. This project should cover the entire IR lifecycle, from initial detection, evidence collection, analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, to final reporting, suitable for a professional portfolio.

resources.title: Blue Team Labs Online - Incident Response Challenge Walkthrough
Incident Response in the Real World: The Basics

children.name: Career Development & Certifications
children.description: Explore common DFIR career paths, prepare for interviews, and understand relevant industry certifications (e.g., GCIH, GCFA, CySA+, eCIR, CREST). Develop strategies for continuous learning, professional networking, and personal branding.

resources.title: Top DFIR Certifications for Your Career
How To Get Into DFIR (Digital Forensics & Incident Response)
Top DFIR Certifications You NEED to Know!
